title: AI Infrastructure Protocol — company scan (Gate 0 contract, as-is map)
description: Output of G0 SCAN. This is the company's operating reality captured as a structured audit, not a survey: every department, every process, and per process the steps, tools, data touched, volume/frequency, hours spent, pains, and handoffs. Gate 0 validates .protocol/company-scan.json against this schema. Gate 0 green requires every department the company named to be present, and every process to have its tools, data, volume, and pains quantified — not just listed.

revenueBand.description: Optional coarse band, e.g. '<1M', '1-10M', '10-50M'. Not required — some clients won't share.

stack.description: Company-wide systems of record named in the kickoff (ERP, CRM, accounting, comms). Per-process tools live under processes[].tools.

namedDepartments.description: The departments the company itself named in the kickoff. coverage.departmentsScanned must cover ALL of these for Gate 0 green — this is the anti-cherry-pick contract.

method.description: How each fact was sourced. 'interview' = the company told us; 'agent-browser'/'scrape' = we inventoried their live tools/sites where permitted; 'artifact' = we read a doc/export they gave us.

permissions.description: What we were permitted to inspect directly. Scraping/automating a tool without this recorded is a Gate 0 red.

departments.description: One entry per operating department. Every department in company.namedDepartments must appear here.

owner.description: Human accountable for this department today.

processes.description: The recurring processes this department runs. A department with zero processes is a Gate 0 red — a department that does nothing was mis-scanned.

coverage.description: Self-reported coverage proof. Gate 0 cross-checks these counts against the actual arrays.

gaps.description: Known blind spots — processes named but not yet fully captured. An empty array asserts full coverage. Never silently omit a gap; a hidden gap surfaces at G1 as an un-dispositionable process.

process.description: One recurring process, fully quantified. Every required field below must carry a real value — 'unknown' volume or 'n/a' hours on a real process is a Gate 0 red, because you cannot rank a backlog you did not measure.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. 'invoice-approval'. G1 blueprint references processes by this id — it must be unique across the whole scan.

trigger.description: What starts this process (e.g. 'customer submits order', 'end of month', 'inbound email').

steps.description: The ordered steps as the company actually does them, in their words. This is the automation surface — vagueness here caps the blueprint's ambition.

actor.description: Role/person who performs this step today.

system.description: Tool the step happens in (must appear in this process's tools[]).

decision.description: True if this step is a judgement/decision point (matters for keep-human vs augment-AI at G1).

tools.description: Every tool/system this process touches. Where permitted and inventoried via agent-browser/scrape, mark inspected:true.

hasApi.description: Does it expose an API/webhook? Drives feasibility of full automation at G1.

inspected.description: True if we inventoried it live (agent-browser/scrape) rather than only hearing about it.

monthlyCost.description: Seat/subscription cost, if known — feeds G4 unit economics.

data.description: Every data object this process reads or writes. Sensitivity drives which processes route through Pillar ⑤ Security at build time.

locatedIn.description: Which tool/system holds it (should match a tools[].name).

volume.description: How often this process runs. Required and numeric — the whole backlog ranking is impact-weighted by volume × hours.

hours.description: Human hours this process consumes. This is the fuel for impact scoring and G4's 'cost taken out' number.

loadedHourlyCost.description: Fully-loaded €/hour for the people doing it, if known — turns hours into euros for G4.

pains.description: Concrete pain points: errors, delays, rework, bottlenecks, things people hate. Each must be specific enough to design against.

evidence.description: How we know — a quote, a metric, an observed instance. Adjective-only pains are weak input.

handoffs.description: Points where work passes between people/teams/tools. Handoffs are where errors and delays concentrate and where automation pays off most. An empty array asserts a self-contained process — allowed, but rare.

via.description: Channel of the handoff: email, Slack, shared sheet, verbal, ticket, etc.

waitHours.description: Typical idle time the work waits at this handoff.
